units.source_text: 到匂亲王家问病的人甚多，天天门庭若市。

en.t: Many people came to Prince Niou's residence to inquire after his illness, and every day his gate was as crowded as a marketplace.

units.source_text: 几乎无人不到，举世骚扰。

en.t: Almost no one failed to come, and the whole world seemed thrown into commotion.

units.source_text: 此时薰大将想：“他为了一个身份并不高贵的女子之死而闭居在家中哀悼，我倘不去慰问，似乎太乖戾了。”

en.t: At this, General Kaoru thought, "He has shut himself away at home in mourning over the death of a woman of no very exalted rank; if I do not go to offer sympathy, it would seem too perverse."

units.source_text: 便前往访问。

en.t: So he went to call on him.

units.source_text: 此时有一位式部卿亲王逝世，薰大将为这叔父服丧，穿着淡墨色丧服。

en.t: Around this time a Prince of the Ministry of Ceremonial had died, and General Kaoru was in mourning for this uncle, wearing pale ink colored mourning robes.

units.source_text: 但他心中只当作为他所悼惜的浮舟服丧，色彩倒很相称。

en.t: But in his heart he treated it as mourning for Ukifune, whom he grieved for, and the color suited him all the more.

units.source_text: 他的面庞稍稍瘦削，然而相貌更增俊俏。

en.t: His face had grown a little thin, yet his looks had become even more handsome.

units.source_text: 别的问病人听见薰大将来，全都退出。

en.t: When the other visitors heard that General Kaoru had arrived, they all withdrew.

units.source_text: 这正是幽静的夕暮时分。

en.t: It was just the quiet hour of evening.

units.source_text: 匂亲王并非常常躺卧在床。

en.t: Prince Niou was not constantly lying in bed.

units.source_text: 疏远的人虽一概不见，一向出入帘内的人则并不拒绝会面。

en.t: Although he refused to see anyone distant from him, he did not decline meetings with those who regularly came and went inside the curtains.

units.source_text: 只是和薰大将相见有些顾虑，颇觉不好意思。

en.t: Only about meeting General Kaoru did he have some misgivings, and he felt rather embarrassed.

units.source_text: 一看到他，未曾开言，眼泪便欲夺眶而出，难于抑制。

en.t: As soon as he saw him, before he had even spoken, tears threatened to spill from his eyes, impossible to hold back.

units.source_text: 好容易镇静下来，说道：“我其实并无大病，只是别人都说这病非要小心谨慎不可。

en.t: At last he composed himself and said, "In truth I am not seriously ill; it is only that everyone says this illness must be treated with the greatest care.

units.source_text: 父皇与母后也非常替我担心，真不敢当。

en.t: My imperial father and my mother are also deeply worried for me, which is more than I deserve.

units.source_text: 我实在是看见世事无常，不胜感伤耳。”

en.t: I am simply overwhelmed with sorrow at seeing how impermanent worldly things are."

units.source_text: 眼中泪如泉涌，他想避人注意，连忙举袖揩拭，但泪珠已经纷纷落下。

en.t: Tears welled from his eyes like a spring; wishing to avoid notice, he quickly raised his sleeve to wipe them away, but the drops had already fallen one after another.

units.source_text: 他觉得不好意思，但念薰大将未必想到这眼泪是为浮舟流的，只是笑我怯弱如同儿女而已。

en.t: He felt ashamed, but thought that General Kaoru would hardly guess these tears were being shed for Ukifune and would merely laugh at him for being as timid as a woman.

units.source_text: 便觉可耻。

en.t: That made him feel disgraced.

units.source_text: 但薰大将想道：“果然如此！

en.t: But General Kaoru thought, "So it was true after all!

units.source_text: 他一直在为浮舟悲伤。

en.t: He has been grieving for Ukifune all this time.

units.source_text: 不知两人几时开始往来的。

en.t: I wonder when the two of them began seeing each other.

units.source_text: 数月以来，他常在笑我是个大傻瓜吧。”

en.t: For these past several months, he must often have been laughing at me as a great fool."

units.source_text: 这样一想，他对浮舟的哀悼之情便忘怀了。

en.t: Once he thought this, his mourning feelings for Ukifune slipped from his mind.

units.source_text: 匂亲王察看他的神色，想道：“此人何等冷酷无情！

en.t: Prince Niou studied his expression and thought, "How cold and heartless this man is!

units.source_text: 凡人胸中怀抱哀愁之时，即使其哀愁不是为了死别，看到空中飞鸣的鸟也会引起悲伤之情的。

en.t: When people carry sorrow in their hearts, even if that sorrow is not from parting by death, the sight of birds flying and crying in the sky can stir their grief.

units.source_text: 我今无端如此伤心哭泣，如果他察知我的心事，不会不感动而流下同情之泪的。

en.t: Now I am weeping so bitterly without any apparent cause; if he understood what is in my heart, he could not help being moved and shedding tears of sympathy.

units.source_text: 只因此人深悟人世无常之理，所以泰然无动于衷。”

en.t: It is only because he has deeply grasped the truth of life's impermanence that he remains so calm and unmoved."

units.source_text: 便觉此人可羡可喜，把他看作美人曾经倚靠过的“青松柱”。

en.t: Then he found this man both enviable and pleasing, seeing him as the "green pine pillar" on which the beautiful woman had once leaned.

units.source_text: 他想象薰大将与浮舟相对之状，觉得此人正是死者的遗念。

en.t: Imagining General Kaoru facing Ukifune, he felt that this man was truly the living remembrance left by the dead woman.
